title: The owner panel — one container over ten capabilities
why: ALivePanel is the last salon-shaped owner panel, and it has already begun retiring itself: its first statement hands SaaS manager roles to `ASaasOwnerPanel` (S-030 L34904, S-096 L31557), so the ten-tab strip is only what the single-salon branch on the legacy proxy still draws. Two owner panels is one too many under ONE MAYA. What the container hard-codes is presentation, not authority — the code heads the block «tab bar (permission-filtered)» and annotates it «Сервер всё равно гейтит». Each tab does carry a `show:(p,i)` predicate over the legacy `__mePerms` shape, but the `avail` filter above them settles the common cases by itself: Аналитика is shown unconditionally, an owner is given every tab regardless of permissions, a non-owner is never given Отчёт, and the per-tab predicate decides only what is left. Removing the container therefore changes what the client draws, not what the server permits — the endpoints behind these tabs re-derive role and answer 403 on their own, the one documented exception being the broadcast tab's template catalogue, which is served before any panel auth. The work that does not vanish with the container is translating that `__mePerms` shape into tenant entitlements.
disappear: Both renderings of ALivePanel — the PWA nav-stack owner panel (S-030, `сайт и приложение/app.html`) and the maya-os-site business screen (S-096) — and with them the client-side tab-visibility machinery: the `avail` filter and the ten per-tab `show:(p,i)` predicates over legacy `__mePerms`. That machinery is a presentation filter, not a gate: no capability disappears with the container, and nothing the server refuses today becomes permitted because the tab bar is gone.
remain: All ten capabilities the panel hosts: analytics, daily report, waitlist, reviews, the eight-job lifecycle catalogue (reactivation, birthday, cycle, reviews, loyalty, subscriptions, referral, leads), broadcast, team, loyalty redeem, schedule, and the founder-only MAYA tab. They do not remain as tabs — each becomes a capability that is asked for or a widget the answer carries, and the founder MAYA tab leaves primary navigation altogether, kept as a platform capability behind verified-session and platform authority rather than folded in beside the others. Three of the ten are already thinner than their tab suggests: the job-run action answers 410 with a pointer to its canonical replacement, the team list returns an empty roster with the same kind of pointer (its other modes 410), and the redemption counter still looks a code up but is refused at confirm with 409 «Погашение через старый контур отключено». The return is contingent rather than automatic: a capability whose key is left unmapped or `restricted` derives a STEP_UP_VERIFIED floor, which is unreachable today, and is then withheld rather than re-surfaced. Where the ten land is the open question — both rows carry successor `MERGE_TARGET — the surface it folds into, to be named`, source `REQUIRES SIGNATURE`, and naming that target is the signature this group asks for. The capability list itself is evidence-backed (inventory capabilities), and neither panel retires before parity: `RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16`.
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH, on two grounds rather than one. First, parity: six of the ten have no counterpart in `ASaasOwnerPanel`'s nine tabs — report, waitlist, reviews, the job catalogue, broadcast, redeem (legacy `ALL_TABS` L31560-31600 against the SaaS `TABS` L30829-30839) — so a merge that simply points the owner at the SaaS panel drops the lifecycle-marketing surface and the redemption path. Calibrated honestly, three of those six are already part-notional on the legacy contour (the 410 / 410 / 409 above), so what a naive merge deletes is the whole eight-job catalogue plus the live halves of the rest — still the largest single loss in this group. Second, authority: the hazard is not a missing gate today but a looser one tomorrow. `loyalty.legacy-redeem.execute.v1` and `gift-certificates.redemption.execute.v1` sit among the 164 of 221 canonical policy definitions carrying the permissive twelve-role `TENANT_ACTION_ROLES` default, and broadcast's canonical key `communication.bulk-campaign.execute.v1` is ALLOW with approval requirement NONE across twelve roles including CLIENT and CUSTOMER (GAP-BULK-SEND-DIRECT, still open). Re-parenting redeem or broadcast onto those keys trades a stricter legacy gate for a weaker canonical one, and any approval on that path is role-gated, not separation of duties. That is why approval stays conditional: no panel-hosted capability is re-parented ahead of the server-side gate meant to hold it. Third and smaller: the `__mePerms` → tenant-entitlement translation, where a mistranslation shows the wrong role the wrong tile, and the merge target is still unnamed while both rows sit on primary navigation, so the K16 parity check has nothing concrete to run against yet.
user_impact: The owner and the masters/managers who share the legacy panel notice this one — but only on the legacy single-salon branch. ALivePanel's first statement (app.html L34904 / maya-os-site L31557) hands SaaS manager roles to ASaasOwnerPanel, so a tenant manager already sees the nine-tab SaaS panel today; the ten-tab strip — Аналитика, Расписание, Отчёт, Лист ожидания, Отзывы, Задачи, Рассылка, Команда, Гашение plus the founder-only MAYA tab — is what the live salon on the legacy proxy sees, and it is permission-filtered, so only a founder-owner ever sees all ten (app.html's `avail` filter L37174-37182 shows Аналитика unconditionally and gives any owner every tab). Afterwards there is no strip, and each capability is asked for in chat. The real, felt risk is the contents, not the container: six of those tabs (report, waitlist, reviews, jobs, broadcast, redeem) have no counterpart in ASaasOwnerPanel's TABS (L30829-30838), so if the merge target is taken to be the SaaS panel the owner loses the eight-job lifecycle-marketing catalogue and the code-redemption counter path. Honest calibration: three of the six are already part-notional, not two. The `panel_job_run` action (POST /api/panel/job/run) answers 410 with a canonical pointer; /api/panel/team mode=list returns an empty roster with a "canonical_action" pointer and every other mode 410s; and /api/panel/redeem still looks a code up but refuses mode=confirm with 409 «Погашение через старый контур отключено» — the counter can check a code and cannot redeem it. The renderOS() claim holds for S-030 only: in app.html the full-screen `god` route now renders Расходы alone, so the embedded panel tab is the sole reachable renderOS(); in maya-os-site (S-096) the god screen still defaults to its own `os` tab and stays reachable via ?god=1 and the MAYA alert card. And "comes back as a contract-declared widget" is contingent, not given — any of these keys left unmapped or `restricted` derives a STEP_UP_VERIFIED floor, which is unreachable, so it is withheld rather than re-surfaced.
security_impact: Direction is half right. Deleting the container alone is neutral: the client-side filters are visibility filters over a permissions object the server itself issued at /api/panel/me (`__meIsFounder` from is_platform_owner/is_founder, role from canonical_staff_access.panel_role), and the legacy endpoints do re-authenticate and re-derive role — redeem → permissions.redeem 403, daily_report → role != 'owner' 403, reviews → permissions.reviews 403, waitlist and dashboard → permissions.analytics / permissions.dashboard 403, master/overview → is_master 403, the MAYA tab → `_god_gate` canonical-platform authority 403 — and app.html says so in its own comment above the filter («Сервер всё равно гейтит»). Two corrections to the evidence: it is not four tests but ten `show(p,i)` predicates (p.analytics, p.reviews, p.jobs, p.marketing, p.staff, p.redeem besides the four named) plus an `avail` filter that already overrides two of the four — analytics returns true unconditionally, and an owner gets every tab regardless of perms; and "every endpoint re-authenticates" is not literal, since panel_broadcast mode='templates' returns the catalogue before any `_panel_auth` and the client sends that mode with no auth header by design (app.html L35440-35441). salon_stats and salary are not behind these tabs at all — neither string appears in the frontend. The larger correction is "not checks a server gate must now be built to replace": true of the legacy contour, false of the successor, which is exactly why the dossier rates this MEDIUM-HIGH and approves only conditionally. `loyalty.legacy-redeem.execute.v1` and `gift-certificates.redemption.execute.v1` sit among the 164 of 221 canonical policy definitions carrying the permissive twelve-role TENANT_ACTION_ROLES default, and the broadcast tab's canonical contour carries GAP-BULK-SEND-DIRECT (`communication.bulk-campaign.execute.v1`: ALLOW, approvalRequirement NONE, twelve roles including CLIENT and CUSTOMER). Re-parenting redeem or broadcast onto those keys trades a stricter legacy gate for a weaker canonical one, and any approval on that path is role-gated, not separation-of-duties. Tenant scope remains genuinely open as stated, and nothing in these two rows touches consent records or audit trails.
